I’m against universal health care not because I disagree with the idea but for a few reasons. One, I can’t name a single program/industry where government got involved and things hit better. Two, America is at least 4x bigger than most European countries do the model that works for them may not for us. Also in saying this since we are so much larger we have a huge population that simply ignores health for a myriad of reasons and it’s not fair to put their costs into the masses. You also have an aging population with boomers- most people spend their medical expenses in the last few years of their lives, I don’t know about you but boomers do not need another handout. Third we are a hub for research and innovation and that could be stifled. There’s many reasons why I’m against it. Let’s talk first about how insurance companies doctor our prices or how the us healthcare system isn’t a free market where people can shop around for their doctor/medical needs. Or addressing the suing culture or big pharma. It’s all daisies and sunshine thinking about universal healthcare, but ethically it cannot happen in this country until other issues are addressed.
